messages:
annah: Quick sync: NovaCare wants Redwood reachable from their analytics cluster via VPC peering for the POC. They also asked if we can hand over a minimal network diagram for approvals.

diego: Peering is doable but requires CIDR non-overlap and route table edits on both sides. Do they want full mesh or specific subnets only?

annah: They said "cluster subnets only". They run in us-east-1 with 10.20.0.0/16.

mina: We'll need their exact subnet ranges (e.g., 10.20.10.0/24) and the AZs. For peering, steps we need from them:
- Create VPC peering request to account 9876543210 (our peering accepter)
- Provide list of route tables to which we should add routes
- Confirm whether they accept propagated routes from a TGW if they use one

mina: Also note: we prefer not to peer into VPCs with overlapping /16s (common blocker). If they want a least-privilege approach, suggest routing only to host subnets instead of entire VPC.

diego: If they insist on peering and strict egress, remind them that our serving instances still need outbound DNS and artifact access. For peering, packets will flow directly so we must provide the IPs of our pool instances or a small CIDR we'll announce to them.

annah: Can we provide a small announcement CIDR for the POC?

mina: For hosted Dedicated pools we usually announce a /27 per region for control-plane egress and model fetch. For customer-managed Dedicated (deployed into their account) we don't announce; instead they control the subnets. For this NovaCare POC (hosted Dedicated), we can provide the /27.

diego: Notes for their firewall team: allow outbound TCP 443 to our announced CIDR and allow DNS (UDP 53) to their resolver — or we can support DNS over TLS if they prefer.

infra-bot: Step created: peering-request-template posted to Slack at 1797123468 by mina.

annah: I put together the minimal diagram text for their approvers: 
- NovaCare VPC (10.20.0.0/16)
  - analytics-subnet-a (10.20.10.0/24)
  - analytics-subnet-b (10.20.11.0/24)
- Redwood Dedicated pool (hosted account) announces POC CIDR 172.31.64.0/27
- VPC peering between NovaCare VPC and Redwood-hosted-network: specific routes only to analytics subnets
- Security groups: NovaCare SG allow outbound 443 to 172.31.64.0/27; Redwood SG allow inbound 443 from 10.20.10.0/24 and 10.20.11.0/24

annah: I'll attach that as a PNG in the email but here's the plaintext for now.

mina: Add a checklist item: confirm whether their infra requires RPKI or prefix validation on the peering side. Sometimes corporate netops flags unknown prefixes.

diego: About auth: they asked if OAuth / short-lived tokens supported. We can issue short-lived tokens for the POC via our SSO integration; otherwise standard API keys are fine. Short-lived tokens add complexity but better for tight security.

annah: Security wants an answer on logs and audit.

security-bot: We provide request logs for the POC with token redaction. Retention: 30d by default for POC, extendable. Questionnaire link: https://redwoodhq.example/sales/sec-qa/novacare

mina: Possible blocker: if they have strict ingress-only ACLs on peering, our SGs must be exact. We'll need the specific port ranges from their netops.

diego: Recommended curl test once peering is up:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health -v
# expect 200 and {"status":"ok"}

annah: Action items:
- get exact subnet CIDRs and route table IDs from NovaCare (annah)
- share POC announced CIDR & firewall allowlist (mina)
- send minimal network diagram + peering steps email (annah)
- decide on API auth (short-lived token vs API key) after security team review (diego + security)

infra-bot: note: peering-request-template: https://redwoodhq.example/internal/peering-templates#minimal-peering

diego: I'll prepare the quick SOW line about peering and that networking changes are customer-managed.

annah: Thanks team, I'll follow up after their netops call tomorrow. :eyes:
